mentor.glaubwuerdigkeit.more: If households and firms do not trust the central bank to bring inflation down, they raise prices and wages as a precaution. Credibility builds slowly and is lost quickly. Experts broadly agree that anchored expectations make fighting inflation easier.
mentor.glaubwuerdigkeit.short: Trust in the central bank is low. Expectations are drifting away from the target.
mentor.kapital.more: Capital grows with trust in the government and a majority in parliament. Small, local projects cost less than nationwide ones. Leaving events unanswered also costs approval.
mentor.kapital.more2: Capital grows on the first of every month and is needed for laws, negotiations and answers to events. Spend it all at once and you cannot react to a crisis. A talk with a parliamentary group costs 1, a law often ten times as much; cheap steps first.
mentor.kapital.short: Your political capital is almost used up. Every change costs some of it; set priorities.
mentor.kapital.short2: Your capital is scarce. Save first, then spend with purpose.
mentor.lira-schwach.more: A weak currency makes imported energy and intermediate goods more expensive. That raises inflation with a delay of a few weeks to months. Exporters, on the other hand, benefit.
mentor.lira-schwach.short: The lira has lost more than inflation explains. Imports become more expensive, and that reaches prices.
mentor.mehrheit.more: You can buy votes (this costs capital and creates a promise that will be called in later) or win partners whose offers arrive as events. Whoever breaks promises loses partners.
mentor.mehrheit.short: Your camp is about {n} votes short of a majority. That makes laws expensive and uncertain.
mentor.partner-wackelt.more: A partner who leaves takes its seats along. Loyalty grows with kept promises and a talk (1 capital) and falls with putting off and breaking promises. Under “People and promises” you can see what it wants.
mentor.realzins-hoch.more: The real rate is the policy rate minus expected inflation. When it is high, saving pays more than borrowing. That dampens consumption and investment and so, over time, inflation. It usually reaches demand only after six to eighteen months, but the currency quickly. The game simplifies banks and lending into a single relationship.
mentor.realzins-hoch.short: The real interest rate is high. That slows lending and demand, though only after months.
mentor.realzins-negativ.more: If the policy rate is below expected inflation, money loses value every month. People prefer to buy today, investors pull money out. In the short term this can stimulate the economy; over time prices and the exchange rate usually rise.
mentor.realzins-negativ.short: The real interest rate is negative. Savers lose money; that drives demand and weakens the lira.
mentor.ruhig.more: I will speak up when something happens that is worth understanding. I won't tell you what is right, but how things are connected.
mentor.ruhig.short: No notable connections at the moment. Click a number in the economy file if you want to know something.
mentor.tipp-start.more: The “Infrastructure” layer colours the map by road density and shows individual districts when you zoom in. That way you see where something is missing before you spend money. Every measure can be limited to individual provinces; it then costs less capital and acts locally.
mentor.tipp-start.short: Tip for the first weeks: click on a province. The sheet shows problems, roads and hospitals; “Build here” leads straight to the measures.
mentor.waehler-verstimmt.more: Why: {gruende}. Whoever is angry looks for a different answer at the election. What they want is shown in the “Voters” window.
